name: OpenClaw Memory Curator
description: Curator daemon and CLI that bridges OpenClaw workspace memory into DKG V10's three-layer verifiable memory system (WM → SWM → VM) with maturity tracking, secret redaction, and deterministic promotion gates.

install.usageHint: Run 'curator status' to check DKG node health, then 'curator ingest' to load workspace memory into Working Memory.

security.notes: Reads DKG auth token from ~/.dkg/auth.token (line 2, comment lines stripped). Scans OpenClaw workspace memory files (~/.openclaw/workspace/memory/*.md) and redacts obvious secrets (private keys, API tokens, mnemonic phrases) before any quad leaves the process. No external network egress: the only host contacted is the DKG node it is installed against (127.0.0.1 by default), which the registry contract does not count as egress. ROUND 1 SCOPE: the only declared VM operation reachable solely through the interactive 'curator publish <ka>' command with a y/n confirmation; it is never automatic and all Round-1 flows (ingest, recall, list, share, daemon) operate purely in WM/SWM.

promotionPath: Working Memory artifacts mature to Shared Working Memory when SWM-eligible: reference count >= 3 in later memory files, or an explicit 'share:' frontmatter tag. The daemon's periodic tick (default 5 minutes) auto-shares eligible KAs; swm/share seals by default, making them publish-ready. 'curator share <ka>' remains available for explicit promotion. Verifiable Memory promotion is gated behind the interactive 'curator publish <ka>' CLI command with a y/n confirmation - never automatic. This deterministic WM -> SWM -> VM pipeline keeps promotion auditable and human-controlled.
fitNotes: Advances the LLM-Wiki / autoresearch direction with a deterministic, auditable curation layer between agent workspace memory and DKG memory. First-party adapter work focuses on chat-turn memory; this curator instead ingests the agent's long-lived workspace memory files (Markdown) as provenance-tagged KAs with a maturity lifecycle, secret redaction, and deterministic promotion.
